title: Step 3: Make It a Function
story: Tidy the script. Wrap the report in a function that takes the log file as its argument.
goal: Write a function report FILE that prints the level counts and the top error for FILE. Call it with the first script argument, or app.log when none is given.

files.app.log:
2026-12-01 ERROR x one
2026-12-01 ERROR x one
2026-12-02 INFO ok fine

hints: Use local so the loop variable does not leak out.

report() {
  local f=$1 lvl
  for lvl in INFO WARN ERROR; do
    echo "$lvl $(grep -c " $lvl " "$f")"
  done
  grep ' ERROR ' "$f" | cut -d' ' -f3- | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | sed -E 's/^ +//'
}
report "${1:-app.log}"
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Step 3: Make It a Function”?
solution:
report() {
  local f=$1 lvl
  for lvl in INFO WARN ERROR; do
    echo "$lvl $(grep -c " $lvl " "$f")"
  done
  grep ' ERROR ' "$f" | cut -d' ' -f3- | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | sed -E 's/^ +//'
}
report "${1:-app.log}"
